questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the part of your lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
Move to the part of your lane closest to the traffic control device.
Move to the outside edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of your lane where other drivers can see you most easily.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you as early as possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead is divided.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest danger of a crash between you and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. The biggest danger is cars turning left in front of motorcyclists.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Is not a concern because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.explanation: Improper braking is a major cause of motorcycle crashes. Learning correct braking technique is essential for safe riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: If there are vehicles on both sides of your motorcycle, which lane position is usually safest?
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Good riders change their position based on road and traffic conditions. When vehicles are on both sides, the center lane position is usually safest.

questions.question: What kind of boots or shoes should a rider wear?

options.text: Boots or shoes that end below the ankle.
Boots or shoes that cover the ankle.
Boots or shoes made of soft, flexible material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Boots or shoes that cover the ankle.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes or boots that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They show traffic laws for that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, what happens?

options.text: The effects are less dangerous than either one alone.
The effects are stronger than either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects are stronger than either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, make riding unsafe. Some drugs become much more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle needs _____ maintenance attention.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent maintenance checks than cars. Any problem must be found and fixed before riding on highways or in traffic.

questions.question: Riding directly beside another vehicle is:

options.text: Safe because you are in a separate lane.
Recommended because it blocks the wind.
Not safe because the driver may not see you in their blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not safe because the driver may not see you in their blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride beside other vehicles. You could be in the driver's blind spot. The driver may not see you and could move into your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Only stop if other traffic is coming.
Other vehicles are entering the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely. Wait for all traffic and pedestrians to pass. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Service signs are:
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where you can find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: A passenger should sit:
questions.explanation: Passengers must sit behind the driver. They should hold onto the driver's waist or hips, or use handholds if available. Never sit sideways on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing all the time to stay visible.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping a motorcycle, you should:
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears using the clutch as you slow down or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only look at what is in front of you.
Only look at what is behind you.
Know what is happening in front and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening in front and behind you.
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead, but also check your mirrors often to know what is behind you. You need to be aware of traffic all around you.

questions.question: Unlike other beverages, alcohol:

options.text: Goes into the bloodstream right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goes into the bloodstream right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It goes straight through the stomach and intestine walls into the blood and quickly reaches the brain.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of strong material.

questions.question: If riding during the day, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen during the day. Wear reflective clothing to be seen, even in daylight. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: What gear should your motorcycle be in when you start the engine?
questions.explanation: Always put your motorcycle in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the dashboard that turns on when the engine is ready to start and the motorcycle is in neutral.

questions.question: Why should you use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection?

options.text: To see if drivers behind you notice that you are stopping.
To look for dark clouds that show bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see if drivers behind you notice that you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see vehicles coming up behind you. Make sure drivers see you and are responding to your actions when you stop.

questions.question: What can happen if you turn too fast?

options.text: You may drift into another lane.
You will get through the turn faster.
You will keep better control of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drift into another lane.
questions.explanation: Turning too fast can cause you to drift into another lane or even leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn.

questions.question: What can happen if you lock your brakes?

options.text: It can cause you to lose control.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause you to lose control.
questions.explanation: Locked brakes can cause control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again. If your rear brake locks on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop.

questions.question: What happens if you grab the front brake or jam the rear brake?

options.text: It is the best way to stop in an emergency.
It is the best way to slow down on wet streets.

questions.explanation: Grabbing the front brake or jamming the rear brake can lock your brakes. This causes control problems.

questions.question: What is the safest position in your lane?
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position based on conditions around you.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: Yes, they have blind spots like cars.
No, because motorcycles are smaller than cars.
No, mirrors are not required on motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they have blind spots like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: How should you use the front brake?

options.text: Use it together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use it together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the edge of the road mean?

options.text: It marks the edge of the traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It marks the edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line shows the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of?
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or a similar strong material for the best grip and protection.
